top.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Widen the lazy SimpleCPUOffload walk for slow stores
top.author: pood1e
top.summary: Fixes KV-cache block eviction race by widening the lazy offload scheduler's walk window based on observed CPU store completion lag, reducing stale evictions from ~17% to <1%.

top.title: [Perf] Gemma 4 slot decision: PrefixLM prefill as FA4 / FlashInfer varlen segments
top.author: simon-veitner-redhat
top.summary: Routes prefix-LM full-attention prefill to FA4/FlashInfer varlen kernels instead of Triton unified attention, yielding 3.9–6.1x speedups on H200/B200.

top.title: [Perf] kimi-k3: Extend deferred-finalize push AR+RMSNorm window to 2 MB (M <= 292)
top.author: leonardHONG
top.summary: Extends the AllReduce+RMSNorm fused deferred-finalize push window from 512KiB to 2MiB, covering M≤292 tokens without extra symmetric memory and avoiding standalone MoE finalize fallback.

top.title: [Perf] diffusion/wan: Load the UMT5 text encoder in BF16 by default
top.author: mickqian
top.summary: Changes Wan diffusion pipelines to load the UMT5 text encoder in BF16 instead of FP32 by default, cutting GPU memory usage ~2x while preserving bit-identical results.

top.title: [TRTLLM-16624][fix] Stop specializing the KDA replay acceptance kernel on batch-view alignment
top.author: zhaoyuanh-nvidia
top.summary: Removes 16-byte alignment specialization on three pointer arguments in the KDA replay acceptance kernel to eliminate redundant Triton compilations during mixed prefill/decode batch transitions in serving.

top.title: [None][fix] Log the MXFP8 tactic choice's per-call tuning bounds at debug level
top.author: chenfeiz0326
top.summary: Adds a `quiet` flag to `autotune` to downgrade MXFP8 autotuning start/end logs from info to debug level, cutting log volume from 93 MB to ~1.3 MB and reducing server warmup stall time.

direction.title: [RFC] Fault Tolerance for RL Workloads in vLLM
direction.author: aoshen02
direction.summary: Proposes fault-tolerant handling for online RL loops in vLLM, covering single-node rollout failures in distributed MoE samplers and dead-pod recovery during NCCL-based weight transfer.

direction.title: [RFC]: Grammar-as-a-Drafter (GaaD): Composing Grammar-Forced Tokens with Speculative Decoding
direction.author: maxwillzq
direction.summary: Proposes composing grammar-forced token drafting with speculative decoding (MTP, EAGLE3, DFlash) to eliminate wasted draft budget on deterministic syntax in structured output generation.

direction.title: [Feature] diffusion: Q4 roadmap proposal: fast MiniMax-H3 image ↔ video switching on consumer GPUs
direction.author: WellyXY
direction.summary: Proposes adding fast image↔video model switching on consumer GPUs to avoid ~75–130s reload overhead from stopping/starting separate servers.

items.body:
Stacked on #52827, #52811; only the top commit is new.

Make the gfx950 expert re-placement (`SGLANG_ROCM_MUSE_GFX950_EXPERT_PLACEMENT`) trigger under attention DP.

## Motivation

The re-placement is collective, and its trigger counts the verify rows of the rank's own batch. Under attention DP every rank holds its own batch (or none), so the ranks would reach the threshold at different steps. A DP rank gains from the placement as a TP rank does: the MORI-EP combine waits for the rank whose experts take longest.

- Under attention DP each rank counts its own target-verify row

items.title: [Feat] [AMD] muse-spark: Run the ROCm model under attention DP with MORI-EP experts
items.author: Duyi-Wang
items.summary: The ROCm Muse Spark model only ran with attention TP. Under attention DP with EP over all ranks, a rank reads only the KV of its own requests and holds 256 / EP experts per layer, and the two all-reduces of a layer become one MORI-EP dispatch / combine pair.
items.body:
Run the Muse Spark ROCm model under attention DP (attention TP1 on every rank), with each rank's MoE rows reaching the other ranks' experts through MORI-EP.

## Motivation

The ROCm Muse Spark model only ran with attention TP. Under attention DP with EP over all ranks, a rank reads only the KV of its own requests and holds 256 / EP experts per layer, and the two all-reduces of a layer become one MORI-EP dispatch / combine pair. This is an enablement PR: it makes the layout run correctly and lets a DP rank use the three decode kernels that were limited to the KV head counts of a TP4 / TP8 rank.

## Overview

With AITER fused shared experts and `--enable-expert-parallel` under data parallelism, the naive DP/EP (AG/RS) dispatch
all-gathers the combined `topk_ids`, including the shared-expert columns that mark which EP rank computes each token's
shared experts. Those marks refer to source-local row indices, so after the gather a token's shared experts run on
every rank or on none. GLM-5.2 MXFP4 at DP4 + EP on MI355X answers 0/200 GSM8K questions correctly on main. This PR re-marks
the gathered rows for the local rank after the dispatch.

## Claims

items.author: triple-mu
items.summary: On SM12x, several FA4 kernels fill the K and V shared-memory stages by TMA. The consumer warps read a stage through the generic proxy, and the producer refills it through the async proxy as soon as the stage is released.

## Motivation

On SM12x, several FA4 kernels fill the K and V shared-memory stages by TMA. The consumer warps read a stage through the generic proxy (`ldmatrix`), and the producer refills it through the async proxy as soon as the stage is released. The TMA pipeline counts one arrive per consumer warp, and nothing orders the warp's shared-memory reads before the refill. Under concurrent GPU work a stage can be overwritten while it is still being read, so the same inputs sometimes give a different output.

items.body:
## What

`fused_moe_preprocess` collapses the entire grouped-GEMM preprocess — cast, stable sort, `src2dst`, offsets, counts, block schedule, ~10 launches — into one single-CTA kernel, bit-identical to the `torch.sort` path. It is gated to `n <= FUSED_PREPROCESS_WIN_TOKENS` routed rows, where `n = tokens x top_k`.

The structural ceiling is the sort key: `tl.sort((ids << 12) | offs)` packs the position into **12 bits**, so at most **4096** routed rows — with top-8 routing, **512 concurrent sequences**. Above that the fused path is never taken and the preprocess runs unfused at every layer.

## Overview

On RDNA4 (gfx12), the Triton encoder/prefill attention kernel (`context_attention_fwd`) pads the head dim up to the next power of 2. Vision encoders often use head dim 72 (Qwen3-VL, the SigLIP tower of Gemma-3) or 80 (Qwen2.5-VL), so the QK and PV dots run over 128 lanes, of which 37-44% are padding. #56450 removed that padding with a head-dim blocking, but enabled it only on gfx1151.

**This PR enables the same head-dim blocking on RDNA4 (gfx1200/gfx1201) by changing its gate from `on_gfx1151()` to `on_gfx1151() or on_rdna4()`.** It changes no kernel code and no launch configurat

## Motivation

On a hybrid sliding-window model, a prefix in the HiCache host tier can be loaded back only while its window is also on host. The window host pool is sized from the device split (`--swa-full-tokens-ratio`), while its demand scales with the full-attention host tokens it has to keep reachable (about `(window + page_size) / chunked_prefill_size` of them). Once the window host pool fills, LRU evicts host windows, and those prefixes stop hitting although their full-attention KV is still on host.

`test_glm_fp32_weights_bit_exact_on_rocm` fails on gfx950 after moving to Triton 3.9.

items.title: [Weight Cache] [Intel] Add Level Zero VMM backend for XPU
items.author: AnuSajikumar6264
items.summary: Adds the Intel XPU Level Zero VMM backend — the XPU counterpart of /, mirroring the CUDA VMM path in #46953. It separates a device allocation's physical pages from its virtual address, exports the physical allocation as a dma-buf fd, and lets an unrelated proc…
items.body:
## Summary

Adds the Intel XPU Level Zero VMM backend — the XPU counterpart of `cuda_vmm_utils` / `hip_vmm_utils`, mirroring the CUDA VMM path in #46953.

It separates a device allocation's physical pages from its virtual address, exports the physical allocation as a **dma-buf fd**, and lets an unrelated process import that fd and map the same memory **at an address of its own choosing**. That is the primitive the `vmm_fd` weight-cache transport needs, and XPU had no equivalent, so `vmm_fd` could not be served on an Intel GPU at all.

It also settles the open driver risk recorded in #497

## Overview

vLLM's `AllReduceFusionPass` fuses the TP all-reduce with the following (fused-add) RMSNorm into one FlashInfer kernel. It only does so for tensors up to `FI_ALLREDUCE_FUSION_MAX_SIZE_MB[capability][world_size]`.

On B200 (SM100) at TP8 the cap is **1 MB**: 102 tokens at hidden 5120, 128 at 4096. Every decode batch above that runs an unfused all-reduce followed by a separate `fused_add_rms_norm`.

This PR raises the SM100 TP8 cap to 16 MB. That is 1638 tokens at hidden 5120, still below SM100 TP4 (32 MB) and SM103 TP2/TP4 (64 MB).

`fused_hc_mix` is one persistent grid (one CTA per SM) that synchronises with a software grid barrier built on three int32 counters. items.title: [Perf] scheduler: Skip the min-free-slots delay when the waiting requests fit
items.author: cedarStackOps
items.summary: With, a late request that fits in the free slots is no longer held until the running batch drains. On 1x A100 (, 8 slots, delay 4), its TTFT drops from 10.35 s to 0.14 s (−98.6%).
items.body:
## Summary

With `--min-free-slots-delay`, a late request that fits in the free slots is no longer held until the running batch drains. On 1x A100 (`gpt-oss-20b`, 8 slots, delay 4), its TTFT drops from **10.35 s to 0.14 s (−98.6%)**. Bursts larger than the free slots are still held as before.

## Motivation

`MinFreeSlotsDelayer` (`--min-free-slots-delay N`) holds new prefills while requests are running and fewer than `N` request slots are free, so that admissions are batched instead of trickling in one at a time. It never looks at the waiting queue, so it also holds requests that already fit

items.body:
This fixes loading for NVIDIA's ModelOpt NVFP4 Llama 4 checkpoints, which crash on main.

nvidia/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-NVFP4 stores each layer's 16 experts as one fused tensor, and it stores their block scales the same way. The scale handler in `mllama4.py` expects one scale per expert, so it tries to copy the whole [16, 512, 5120] block-scale tensor into each expert and crashes. We now load 3-D block scales through the path that already loads the fused weights, which transposes and splits them per expert.

items.summary: salts every multimodal request's prefix-cache key with its media digest from the first token, so requests with the same text but different images never share cached KV, not even the text before the first image. The salt guards against one-token media spans, wh…

## Motivation

`bind_multimodal_cache_namespace` salts every multimodal request's prefix-cache key with its media digest from the first token, so requests with the same text but different images never share cached KV, not even the text before the first image. The salt guards against one-token media spans, whose single pad token carries only 62 of the digest's 256 bits. A span covering all of an item's `padding_values()` already writes the full digest into the token ids, so the radix key keeps different media apart without the salt.

## Modifications

- Add `media_spans_carry_identity()`: true

items.title: [Fix] benchmark: Publish complete shared-prefix dataset caches atomically
items.author: yingluobailu
items.summary: Two benchmarks using the same generated-shared-prefix cache can overlap while the first writer is still serializing its rows. Opening the final filename immediately exposes an incomplete pickle.
items.body:
## Motivation

Two benchmarks using the same generated-shared-prefix cache can overlap while the first writer is still serializing its rows. Opening the final filename immediately exposes an incomplete pickle. If writing is interrupted, later runs keep reading that incomplete file and fail before the workload starts.

## Modifications

Write the dataset in a temporary directory on the cache filesystem, close it, then atomically replace the final path. A read that encounters an empty or malformed pickle regenerates the derived dataset. Other I/O errors continue to propagate.

## Accuracy Tests

With `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_LINEAR_HIPBMM=1` (off by default), `AiterHipbMMPerTokenFp8ScaledMMLinearKernel` accepts any K divisible by 16, but it can't compute every such K. ## Overview

Follow-up to #69446 (as offered there). ## Overview

Allow `--engram-config '{"disk_offload": true}'` for Qwen4Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) on ROCm, as `#59958` did for NVIDIA: the 102.4 GB PLE table stays in the checkpoint's safetensors files and each step's rows are read from them, so a 128 GB unified-memory machine (AMD Strix Halo, gfx1151) can serve the model.
The AMD model reuses NVIDIA's `Qwen4ExpPLEDiskOffloadEmbedding` and `stage_checkpoint_rows` (imported); the change is their wiring in `amd/ple_layer.py` and `amd/model_state.py`, a two-line config gate, one docs line and tests. `nvidia/`, `common/` and defaults are unchanged.

items.author: four1er

items.body:
Fixes #9713

## Bug

Rank 0 rewrote `latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt` with `open(..., 'w')` and `latest_train_state.pt` with `shutil.copy`, both in place, so a crash mid-save could leave an empty tracker behind. On restart `read_metadata` then printed `ERROR: Invalid metadata file ... Exiting` and called bare `sys.exit()`, exiting 0, so the job ended without training and a scheduler took it as success. With `--save-retain-interval` an empty tracker also failed every later save with a bare `int()` `ValueError`.

## Fix

- `megatron/training/checkpointing.py`: new `write_text_file_atomically()

items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`EngineCoreProc` hashes each new request's prompt blocks on its input thread while the busy loop waits for the step's model output. Hashing a long prompt is a Python loop that holds the GIL for up to a whole switch interval (5 ms) at a time, so the busy loop notices a finished step late. With data parallelism, every other rank then waits at the next DP sync.

This PR makes the input thread release the GIL after each 1 ms of prompt hashing, and only the input thread.

items.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Treat non-positive fps as unset for video/jpeg and the GLM-GA loader
items.author: yarikama
items.summary: Fixes ZeroDivisionError crashes when non-positive fps values are passed for video/jpeg inputs across multiple model processors, falling back to default fps=1 instead.
items.body:
## Overview

For `video/jpeg` inputs (pre-extracted frames), `VideoMediaIO.load_base64` copies the `fps` from `media_io_kwargs` into the video metadata without checking it, and processors divide by it. With `fps=0`, Qwen3-VL and Muse Spark Open raise `ZeroDivisionError` outside `call_hf_processor`, so the server returns 500. Other processors fail with a 400 whose message is "float division by zero", and a negative or NaN fps silently changes the number of video tokens on several models.

For `video/jpeg`, `fps` is the frame rate of the original video, and a request without it already uses 1.

items.title: [KV Offload] Do not pin SimpleCPUOffload buffers under NVIDIA Confidential Computing
items.author: bfoing
items.summary: fails to start on an H100 in Confidential Computing (CC) mode: it pins its CPU KV buffers with, which the GPU refuses for guest memory under CC. This keeps the buffers unpinned when CC is detected, so the CPU tier works there with pageable copies.
items.body:
## Overview

`SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` fails to start on an H100 in Confidential Computing (CC) mode: it pins its CPU KV buffers with `cudaHostRegister`, which the GPU refuses for guest memory under CC. This keeps the buffers unpinned when CC is detected, so the CPU tier works there with pageable copies.

## Claims

- `vllm serve … --kv-offloading-size N` with `VLLM_USE_SIMPLE_KV_OFFLOAD=1` starts on an H100 in CC mode (it fails at KV cache initialization on main).
- The CPU tier works on that platform: after the GPU prefix cache is cleared, a repeated prompt is loaded back from the CPU tier

items.body:
## Description

trtllm-bench's async client dispatches its whole inbox into request tasks when the benchmark starts. For the rest of the run, `LlmManager.worker` then polled the empty inbox with `await asyncio.sleep(0)`, so the event loop never blocked: the client process kept a core busy and held the GIL most of the time. The LLM API thread that delivers each response to the request coroutines needs the GIL too.

On two-socket Intel hosts with Linux 5.15, like QA's H100 nodes, this starves that thread. CPython restarts a waiting thread's 5 ms switch timeout every time the GIL holder releases

1.4.0rc3, C++ cache transceiver over UCX, hybrid model (48 linear-attention + 16 full-attention layers).

`kv_cache_size` only counts paged KV: 82 to 86 MiB for ~1.3k-token prompts, while each handoff moves ~166 MB because the recurrent state (78 MB per slot) goes over too. So it reads ~48% low.

`rnnCacheFormatter.cpp` never calls `updateKvCacheSize`, though `cacheFormatter.cpp` does.

items.body:
## Summary

On the V1 FSDP path, `update_weights` (actor → rollout engine weight sync) broadcasts the **full parameter set every training step**. Measured cost on Qwen2.5-32B TP8: ~9 s/step, every step, regardless of how few parameters changed. Over hundreds of GRPO steps this is a fixed tax proportional to model size, not to actual weight drift.

## Suggestion

A bucketed delta mode would remove most of this cost:

- hash/checksum per parameter bucket, sync only buckets whose checksum changed (in practice almost none change every step in RL fine-tuning — the update is small relative to init)

items.author: xrennvidia
items.summary: With N > 1, each LM head (main and MTP) projects, scores and differentiates the sequence one N-th at a time, so the fp32 logits are never allocated for the whole sequence. Results match the unchunked head up to rounding and no work is repeated.
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Adds `lm_head_loss_num_chunks` (`--lm-head-loss-num-chunks`, default 1 = off). With N > 1, each LM head (main and MTP) projects, scores and differentiates the sequence one N-th at a time, so the `[seq, batch, vocab]` fp32 logits are never allocated for the whole sequence. Results match the unchunked head up to rounding and no work is repeated.

**Why:** with a large vocabulary the logits set peak memory. For 8192 tokens and a 262k vocabulary, one head holds 8 GiB of logits plus a 4 GiB copy

items.title: Activation checkpointing runs during torch.no_grad()
items.author: sbhavani
items.summary: Activation checkpointing wraps the forward in torch.no_grad but still enters CheckpointFunction, queuing states for a backward recompute that never executes during forward-only RL log-prob computations.
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

`tensor_parallel.checkpoint()` enters `CheckpointFunction` under `torch.no_grad()`. The wrapped forward sees `is_checkpointing() == True` and can queue state for a backward recompute that never runs. 

Miles hit this during forward-only RL log-probability computation. [code](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/f0987cfeb8d358637cddd054e270f757a0dd53cf/megatron/core/tensor_parallel/random.py#L796)

**Steps/Code to reproduce bug**

With a CUDA tensor `x`, run `checkpoint(fn, False, x)` inside `torch.no_grad()`. Have `fn` print `is_checkpointing()`. It prints `True`.

## Purpose

Implement the existing `--check-weight-update-equal` flag for the first actor-to-rollout weight update. Before the first rollout, Vime verifies that the trainer can restore the target-model parameters originally loaded by each vLLM endpoint. ### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8766.

In V1 trainers (`sync` and `colocate_async`), `_compute_advantage()` whitens advantages once over the full sampled batch, whereas `TrainingWorker.train_mini_batch()` splits the batch into `ppo_mini_batch_size` optimizer chunks without re-normalizing per chunk. This PR re-normalizes `mini_batch_td["advantages"]` per optimizer chunk in `TrainingWorker.train_mini_batch()`

items.title: [Bug] TransferQueue drops samples after a 30 s ACK timeout, then compute_log_prob fails with KeyError: 'loss_mask' (Qwen2-7B GSM8K GRPO recipe)
items.author: AmineDiro
items.summary: On verl v0.9.1, verl's own Qwen2-7B-Instruct GRPO GSM8K recipe (the baseline in ) crashed twice on 8x B200, both times on the first training step after a validation pass. Right before the crash, the agent-loop workers log and carry on.
items.body:
## Summary

On verl v0.9.1, verl's own Qwen2-7B-Instruct GRPO GSM8K recipe (the `qwen2-7b-fsdp2.log` baseline in `docs/algo/baseline.md`) crashed twice on 8x B200, both times on the first training step after a validation pass. Right before the crash, the agent-loop workers log `Timeout waiting for data status update ACK from controller after 30s` and carry on. The data was written to storage but the controller never marks it ready, so the trainer later gets an empty batch from TransferQueue and fails with `KeyError: 'loss_mask'` in `compute_log_prob`.

The timeout itself is a slow controller.

The health monitors are paused from the end of a rollout (`finish_rollout`) to the weight update. An engine that dies in that window stays registered in the router and in the engine list. With the fully-async rollout the periodic check does not help either: each resume restarts the first wait (600 s by default), so no periodic check runs when a rollout takes less than that. ### What does this PR do?

Newer torchtitan (e.g. the TPU fork at google-pytorch/torchtitan#201) moved two modules that the TorchTitan engine imports:

## 问题

`ascend` 分支的 `image-build-npu` step（`.buildkite/pipeline-npu-image.yaml`，queue `ascend-a3`）没有指定 `image:`，执行 shell 的 container-0 用的是 Buildkite agent 默认镜像（Alpine，`wget` 是 BusyBox applet）。

当 agent 镜像里没有 `buildctl` 时，step 会走安装分支：

```bash
wget -q "https://gh-proxy.test.osinfra.cn/https://github.com/moby/buildkit/releases/download/${BUILDKIT_VERSION}/buildkit-${BUILDKIT_VERSION}.linux-arm64.tar.gz" -O /tmp/buildkit.tar.gz
```

URL 虽然已经套了 gh-proxy，但 BusyBox wget **不会**为 https 请求向 HTTP 代理发送 `CONNECT`，而是把完整 URL 直接交给代理，失败信息为：

```
wget: error getting response: Resource temporarily unavailable
`
discussion:

items.author: FeiyangP
items.summary: slime forwards Megatron's unchanged, but it saves checkpoint (0-based): with the saved iterations are. Megatron's deletes the previous checkpoint whenever, and none of slime's iterations is ever a multiple of the retain interval.
items.body:
## Problem

Fixes #2532.

slime forwards Megatron's `--save-retain-interval` unchanged, but it saves checkpoint `rollout_id` (0-based): with `--save-interval N` the saved iterations are `N-1, 2N-1, ...`. So each save deletes the one before it, and only the latest checkpoint survives: the opposite of what the option is for. items.title: [algo, trainer, fsdp, megatron, cfg, doc] feat: add topk_rb KL loss (top-k Rao-Blackwellised KL to the reference)
items.author: hiddevandebeek
items.summary: It adds, a KL penalty against the reference policy for. The estimator computes KL(πθ ‖ πref) exactly over the reference top-k tokens plus one tail bucket.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Implements the RFC in #8536. It adds `actor.kl_loss_type: topk_rb`, a KL penalty against the reference policy for `use_kl_loss=True`.

The estimator computes KL(π_θ ‖ π_ref) exactly over the reference top-k tokens plus one tail bucket. The within-tail part is estimated from the sampled token, so the result is an **unbiased** estimate of the full-vocabulary KL gradient at every k, with much lower variance than the single-sample `kl`/`k2`/`low_var_kl`/`k3+` options. It is the per-token Rao-Blackwellised KL of [Amini et al., NeurIPS 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.1063

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Preserve vLLM's `finish_reason="length"` in `TokenOutput.stop_reason`. Today the vLLM rollout server reports `completed` both when generation stops naturally and when the output budget cuts it off. A caller translating this value to the Anthropic Messages API consequently sends `end_turn` for a truncated response, and the client can exit with work still in progress.

### Design and compatibility

Map vLLM's `stop` to `completed` and let `length` pass through the existing fallback. Callers can now return `max_tokens` to Anthropic clients. Abort still maps to `aborted`

Restore bounded layered LoRA collection for FSDP1 layouts with flattened parameters or independently wrapped adapter leaves. Initialize FSDP1 from its real root, recognize original flat-parameter names and leaf prefixes, normalize parameter ownership

items.title: [reward] fix: compare prime_code call-based outputs as plain builtins
items.author: Aarav500
items.summary: In, call-based tests compared the generated function's return value with. The generated code controls that object, so a subclass of or whose always returns got full reward on every call-based task.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8656. In `prime_code`, call-based tests compared the generated function's return value with `output == expected`. The generated code controls that object, so a subclass of `int` or `list` whose `__eq__` always returns `True` got full reward on every call-based task. Swapping the operands doesn't help, because Python tries a subclass's reflected `__eq__` first.

This adds `_to_builtin()` in `prime_code/testing_util.py` and applies it to the output right after the existing `json.dumps(output)` call. It rebuilds the value from plain `None`/`bool`/`int`/`float

### What does this PR do?

Enable a shared Mooncake KV cache pool for vLLM rollout, and turn on Ascend PD disaggregation on top of the existing GPU PD path.

Non-PD rollout attaches one Store connector (`MooncakeStoreConnector` on GPU, `AscendStoreConnector` on NPU). PD rollout keeps the P2P connector and wraps it with the Store connector in a `MultiConnector`.

Ascend PD uses `MooncakeConnectorV2`. `

items.body:
## Problem and behavior

Checkpoint participants each own one GPU, but Ray's default first barrier can enroll every visible GPU and its rendezvous key contains the local ordinal. The engine now owns a device-bound NCCLGroup specialization with a single-device barrier and a logical group key shared across masked/shared ordinal layouts. Allocation, executor-thread broadcast, synchronization and destruction use the engine device. Ordinary Ray groups retain their behavior, and duplicate ownership/topology checks remain. Delta transfers reuse this group and device without changing the wire protocol

## Motivation

`Float16Module.forward` upcasts the last pipeline stage's output to fp32 by default. slime calls the actor with `labels=None`, so the whole `[T, V]` logits tensor is copied to fp32. The LM head GEMM has already rounded these values to bf16, so the copy adds memory but no precision. It is the largest single allocation in a long-context actor step: 40,960 tokens × 248,320 vocabulary is about 41 GB in fp32 versus 20 GB in bf16.

## Problem

For `k3` and `low_var_kl`, `compute_approx_kl` evaluates `exp(x) - 1 - x`, where `x = log_probs_base - log_probs`. This expression is nonnegative in real arithmetic, but subtracting 1 from a float32 exponential can erase the small KL term or make it negative when the policies are close.

With valid finite log-probabilities near -0.1, I reproduced a value of -1.4901161e-8 where an 80-digit reference gives 4.9986626e-11. The helper feeds the reported KL term and configured KL loss/reward paths; the Search-R1 example selects `low_var_kl` with a nonzero KL-loss coefficient.

## Problem

With `--partial-rollout`, a sample aborted mid-generation goes back to the data buffer and is resumed later. `generate()` resumes it with a `max_new_tokens` budget reduced by `sample.response_length` and appends the new tokens after the existing response, so the request must be conditioned on that response.

For samples with images, the request is built as:

```python
payload["image_data"] = [...]
payload["text"] = sample.prompt
```

`sample.prompt` does not include the response generated so far, so SGLang starts a fresh response from the prompt. The new tokens are then appended af

items.title: fix(data): give uniform reward groups exactly zero advantage
items.author: saloni-garg
items.summary: When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about …
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

Small reproduction on current main (a group of 16 rollouts that all scored 0.3, `grpo` with `grpo_std_normalization`):

-
discussion: The nonzero advantages for uniform fractional rewards reproduce on `main`. I ran the grouped-reward tests at `0063710` on CPU with PyTorch 2.13.0: uniform groups produce exact zeros, and the mixed-group and nonfinite-reward cases pass too.
Thank you for checking, and for reproducing it on main as well. Glad the tests hold up on your side too. Happy to run anything else you would like to see here.

items.author: Domin-Focus
items.summary: Both are falsy, so the guard treats them as a missing label, and every correct response scores 0 under. Under GRPO, a group where every sample gets 0 gives no learning signal for that prompt.
items.body:
## Problem

`grade_answer_verl` (`slime/rollout/rm_hub/math_utils.py:485`) starts with:

```python
if not ground_truth:

```

Labels are passed through from the dataset as-is (`slime/utils/data.py:272`), so a zero answer arrives as `0` or `0.0`. Both are falsy, so the guard treats them as a missing label, and every correct `\boxed{0}` response scores 0 under `rm_type=math`. Under GRPO, a group where every sample gets 0 gives no learning signal for that prompt.

## Summary

Allow a failed Megatron training job to restart on the same Ray cluster while retaining healthy SGLang engines, routers, and accepted rollout data. The new trainer can change its parallel layout and replay the batches after the last committed checkpoint without regenerating samples or repeating accepted reward postprocessing.

Replay uses Straw storage (`--rollout-data-transport straw`) or per-rollout debug dumps (`--save-debug-rollout-data` with `{rollout_id}` in the path). Internal serving retention does not require the legacy `--use-fault-tolerance` flag.

items.author: chaoworks
items.summary: Disk-delta sync can report success while leaving the model's indexed weights unchanged when a checkpoint directory contains unreferenced safetensors files with duplicate tensor names. Both the trainer's baseline reader and the engine's local checkpoint writer …
items.body:
Disk-delta sync can report success while leaving the model's indexed weights unchanged when a checkpoint directory contains unreferenced safetensors files with duplicate tensor names. Both the trainer's baseline reader and the engine's local checkpoint writer scan every safetensors file, so a stale file visited last can override the indexed tensor location. The sender and receiver can agree on that stale file, pass checksum verification, and still leave the weights used for model reload untouched.

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ

## Background

`generate_and_rm_group` supports custom generation that fans one input out into `list[Sample]`, so a fully-async task can return `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

Fixes #2409

## Problem

`compute_gpqa_reward` falls back to a text match when no option letter can be extracted from the reply. That fallback (1) appended a one-letter gold label as answer text, and (2) searched each candidate as a raw substring of the normalized reply. A reply that never answers, for example `I'm sorry, but I can't help with that.`, therefore scored 1.0 whenever the gold letter (`a`, `b`, `c`) occurred inside a word, and a short numeric choice such as `11` matched inside `2011` or `111`.

## Approach

- A one-character label that is a valid option letter is no longer added t

items.title: fix: restore actor weights before initial rollout sync
items.author: tengeel
items.summary: Without, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.
items.body:
## Problem

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

Without `--offload-train`, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.

For one resumed run:

| | rollout logprob | reference logprob | actor logprob |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Before | -0.1106 | -0.1111 | -0.1471 |
| After | -0.1088 | -0.1421 | -0.1

items.author: LOGO127
items.summary: Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path. Under CUDA autocast, can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32.
items.body:
## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

For example, total length 9 and response length 3 at CP=2 leave rank 0 with no response predictions, so indexing its last reward raises IndexError. If rank 0 owns earlier response predictions, the reward is instead attached to the wrong time step.

Use the existing CP token offsets to find the shard containing the final response token. CP=1 retains the existing behavior, and the per-token KL reward remains unchanged.

Includes @aoshen02's local multi-turn smoke test (aoshen02/vime#4) with his agreement, then makes the loop actually train on ROCm/MI355X.

## Why it couldn't train

The smoke test runs end to end but cannot learn on any platform:

```
--n-samples-per-prompt 1
--rollout-temperature 0.0
```

GRPO computes its advantage within a prompt's sample group. One sample gives an advantage of identically zero; greedy decoding makes n samples identical, so group variance is zero too. Both have to change — fixing either alone still gives no gradient.

## What's in here

- Working GRPO default

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

## Fix

Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

## Background

In the agentic rollout path, each agent turn sends a request to SGLang through the SGLang router. When a request is cancelled or hits the client-side read timeout, Slime must explicitly abort the corresponding SGLang request to release its scheduler slot and KV-cache resources.
